description:
High finding on the oracle carry digest, REPRODUCED by the controller on origin/develop 2026-10-23: _project/scripts/oracle_reviewers/protocol.py file_patches iterates body.splitlines(), which splits on form feed and other control characters, and the hunk counts are discarded from the hashed header. Two different patches therefore hash identically: a diff adding the source lines 'permissions = READ' and '+WRITE' (hunk +1,2; Python gives permissions == 1) and a diff adding the single line 'permissions = READ<FF>+WRITE' (hunk +1,1; Python gives permissions == 3) produce equal file_patches, so plan_round can return CARRY and a prior SHIP covers behavior-changing edits without review.

DECISION GATE: split only on the newline character that git uses for diff lines (body.split('\n')) and keep every other byte; include each hunk's old and new line counts in the hashed header in a rebase-stable way (counts are not absolute positions, so a plain rebase keeps them). Verify the existing rebase tests (a hunk at line 1 versus line 9 equal) and the PR 2769 replay still pass unchanged; if including counts breaks either, stop and report options instead of loosening a test.
